children: wants the AI spending boom to keep paying after the servers arrive. The hardware supplier is expanding its AI-security and recovery offerings, giving customers more reasons to spend on protecting the systems they have bought. Shares fell 1.92% to $492.32 at 11:00 a.m. ET on October 28. The commercial pitch is straightforward: selling the equipment opens the door; keeping it secure could bring customers back.

The opportunity starts with a sizable customer base. Dell reported $16.4 billion in AI-optimized server revenue and $4.9 billion in storage revenue within its $31.8 billion infrastructure business in the latest quarter. Resilience Operations for AI is now available, with further storage-software and integration releases scheduled for November and December. Those deployments could create demand for ongoing protection and recovery services, although Dell has not put a revenue figure on the new offerings.

The valuation leaves Dell with something to prove. GuruFocus shows a GF Score of 71 out of 100 and a price-to-earnings ratio of 28.58, while its radar chart places growth and profitability ahead of valuation and momentum. That combination suggests strong operating performance may already carry a meaningful price tag. The next test is whether Dell can deliver the scheduled releases, persuade customers to buy additional services and turn those purchases into renewals and stronger infrastructure margins.

title: Dell Stocks Decline With New AI Recovery Services
